about: A dungeon-crawl sequel in the Zork tradition. You wake from a dream of a silver-haired old man who says you must prove yourself worthy. You then explore a dark underground empire with your old brass lantern, past a sword in a rock, a sunlit cliff oasis and an underground sea.

done.why: I played a short sample to judge the prose and stopped before any goal or ending came up.

moments.note: The lantern description reads like an old friend who would rather not have come.
The rock description says it 'has the look of a thing that has been invited many times'.
Moving south put me in the dark with a grue warning, so I needed to light the lamp.

wished: I wished I could have asked about the old man or found some sign of the final test.

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: A wry line that made the sword in the rock feel fresh.

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come.

fun.why: I explored only a few rooms, and what I read was pleasant.

engagement.why: The opening dream sets up a goal, but I didn't go far enough to feel it.

difficulty.why: Nothing blocked me except the dark, and the lamp solved that.

interestingness.why: The setting is a familiar Zork-style one, and the added details gave it character.

prose.why: The newly written descriptions of the lantern and the rock are sharp and witty. The room text that looks borrowed is plainer by comparison.
